- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >+5% from prior day), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above prior peak for next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.33) and price is trending down, model underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to avoid premature bottoming.
- Model frequently underestimates late-period (last 5–7 days) price movements; apply 1–2% upward bias to final 5–7 forecast days if sentiment is neutral or positive.
- When sentiment shifts from negative to positive mid-period, model lags in adjusting; add 0.5–1.0% to forecast from day 10 onward if sentiment >0.50.
- If model forecast is consistently 1–2% below true outcome over 3–5 days, apply upward bias of 1.5–2.5% for next 3 days if sentiment remains positive.
- Avoid forecasting sharp downward moves unless sentiment is >0.75; if sentiment <0.3, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% to avoid overcorrection.
